html:
The Tsawwassen are a Coast Salish people of the Fraser River delta in British Columbia, on the point just north of the border with the United States. Their name means "land facing the sea", and they speak Hun'qumi'num, a dialect of Halkomelem.

They fished for salmon in the Fraser and its delta, gathered shellfish on the tidal flats and travelled by canoe to fishing and berry grounds across the Strait of Georgia. Smallpox reached them in the late 1700s, before they ever met Europeans face to face. After British Columbia joined Canada they were confined to a small reserve, and much of their shore was later used for a ferry terminal and the Roberts Bank coal port. In 2009 the Tsawwassen First Nation's treaty came into force, the first modern treaty in an urban area of the province. Their neighbours include the Musqueam and the Semiahmoo.
